title: The Untold Story of Paul the Apostle
paragraphs: The Untold Story of Paul the Apostle
He held the coats while they crushed a man to death.
And somewhere in the middle of the screaming, a young Pharisee named Saul watched with approval.
The Greek word used there is “συνευδοκῶν” (syneudokōn).
It means more than passive agreement.
Saul was not accidentally near evil.
He believed he was serving God through it.
That is what makes his story terrifying.
And maybe that is why so many people secretly relate to him.
But because they know what it feels like to be violently wrong while believing they are spiritually right.
This is the untold story of Paul the Apostle.
Not the sanitized Sunday school summary.
But the story of a broken man whose past never stopped haunting him… and whose encounter with Jesus Christ became one of the greatest testimonies of grace the world has ever known.
Because before he became Paul the Apostle…
And religion had made him dangerous.
Philippians 3:5-6 reveals how Saul saw himself before Christ:
“Circumcised the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee; as to zeal, persecuting the church…”
The phrase “Hebrew of Hebrews” comes from the Greek:
It was a declaration of pedigree.
Educated under Gamaliel according to Acts 22:3.
That should shake every religious person reading this.
You can memorize Scripture and still miss the Messiah standing in front of you.
You can defend theology while resisting the Holy Spirit.
You can appear righteous publicly while being spiritually blind internally.
Saul genuinely believed Christianity was blasphemy.
He saw followers of Jesus as dangerous deceivers threatening covenant purity.
“But Saul was ravaging the church, and entering house after house, he dragged off men and women and committed them to prison.”
It was used for wild beasts tearing apart prey.
Luke intentionally paints Saul like a spiritual predator.
Some of you know exactly what religious cruelty feels like.
Maybe someone used Scripture to control instead of heal.
Maybe people claiming to represent God became the reason you ran from Him.
Paul understood that darkness better than most preachers ever will.
Because he used to be part of it.

“Now as he went on his way, he approached Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven shone around him. And falling to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?’ And he said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.’”
The name Jesus says there in Greek:
Christ identifies Himself so deeply with His followers that their suffering becomes His suffering.
That means every tear cried in secret…
Saul thought he was fighting Christians.
He was actually fighting Christ Himself.
The confident Pharisee needed to be led by the hand.
The man who thought he could see spiritually discovered he had been blind the entire time.
Because sometimes God must break our certainty before He can heal our soul.
For three days Saul sat in darkness.
Only the unbearable realization that the Jesus he hated was truly the Messiah.
Can you imagine the horror flooding his mind?
He had been persecuting the Son of God.
Some people reading this know exactly what conviction feels like.
That moment where God exposes what pride kept hidden.
Where you realize you need mercy more than reputation.
And yet this is where the Gospel becomes almost unbelievable.
That is the scandal of grace.
Because if most people were Jesus, Saul would have been struck dead.
“He is a chosen instrument of Mine…”
Imagine hearing that after murdering believers.
Imagine God saying your worst chapter is not the end of your story.
Somebody reading this has spent years believing they are too dirty for God.
Because Christianity is not about good people earning mercy.
It is about guilty people receiving grace.
The Hebrew concept behind grace is often connected to “חֵן” (chen).
Years later, he still called himself:
Notice he did not say “I was.”
Paul carried deep awareness of what grace rescued him from.
But because forgiven people never fully get over mercy.
That is why his writings burn with emotional intensity.
When Paul wrote about grace, he was not writing theory.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith.”
Paul knew exactly what it meant to be rescued from himself.
And maybe this is the part most people never talk about:
Paul still suffered deeply after conversion.
Following Jesus did not erase hardship.
2 Corinthians 11 reads almost like a trauma journal.
And yet Paul kept preaching Christ.
Because once you know Jesus is truly alive…
Nothing else matters the same anymore.
Paul had seen the risen Christ.
The Greek word for witness is “μάρτυς” (martys).
It eventually became the root for the English word martyr.
Because early believers understood witnessing for Christ could cost them everything.
And through the Holy Spirit, the former enemy of Christianity became one of its greatest defenders.
Letters that still transform millions of lives today.
But perhaps the most heartbreaking detail about Paul is this:
Three times Paul begged for it to leave.
Some of you are angry because God did not remove your thorn.
But what if the thorn became the thing keeping you dependent on Christ?
Paul learned that weakness was not the end of usefulness.
In God’s kingdom, broken vessels still carry glory.
Especially those exhausted from pretending to be perfect.
Yet listen to his final confidence in 2 Timothy 4:7:
“I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.”
And maybe that is the untold story people desperately need right now.
The Gospel is still transforming Sauls into Pauls.
Jesus Christ is still rewriting lives.
And maybe the reason this story hurts so deeply is because many people see themselves in both sides of Paul.
The part that ran from God.
And the part still hoping grace can somehow win.
“Where sin increased, grace abounded all the more.”
Grace is greater than your worst chapter.
Christ is stronger than your darkest history.
And the cross was always bigger than your failure.
Maybe you have been pretending publicly while dying privately.
Maybe guilt has chained your mind for years.
Maybe you secretly wonder if God could still want someone like you.
Yes, Jesus Christ still changes human hearts.
This hit harder than you expected.
And if someone you love feels too far gone for grace… send this to them.
The same God who blinded Saul on the road to Damascus is still interrupting lives today.
